summary: With a charged cursed Bell of Opening used outside the invocation square while the hero is not swallowed, apply.c:use_bell calls mkundead. JavaScript currently records an unported gap and wakes nearby monsters, so the undead swarm and its random calls are missing. Port mkroom.c:mkundead and wire both source callers; morguemon is already ported.

source.branch: A charged Bell of Opening is applied; the hero is not swallowed and the bell is cursed. apply.c:use_bell consumes a charge, calls mkundead(&mm, FALSE, NO_MINVENT), then wakes nearby monsters. The general mkundead function also has a corpse-revival arm when revive_corpses is true.
callers: apply.c:use_bell 1253-1269 -> js/apply.js: use_bell currently calls note_unported("minion.c mkundead") and then continues to wake_nearby; wire the real mkroom.c implementation here.
spell.c:deadbook 323 -> js/spell.js:raise_dead currently records note_unported("mkroom.c mkundead"); wire the same function here and preserve revive_corpses=true behavior.
dependencies: mkundead 454-473 draws the swarm count with rnd(5), calls morguemon for each attempt, uses enexto to find a square, optionally checks sobj_at/revive when revive_corpses is true, calls makemon with discarded return, and sets level.flags.graveyard. js/mkroom.js:morguemon already ports morguemon; reuse it.

For revive_corpses=true from spell.c:deadbook, preserve the consumed revive return. zap.c:revive is already ported in js/zap.js and returns a monster or null, so the caller must test its truth value. The cursed Bell caller passes FALSE and skips this branch.
Reuse the existing level_difficulty, enexto, sobj_at, makemon runtime, and wake_nearby implementations; retain source order and RNG calls.

evidence: The exact examined revision is 84d84e111155ac834c43327b7c696055df294349; its submodule gitlink and local checkout both resolve to 16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4. The saved v24 evaluation is challenges/evaluations/20261006225046-v24.json. Its queue entry has 35 recorded steps, 31/35 screens, 2202/2362 RNG calls, 35/35 cursors, and four remaining screens.

The first divergence is segment 0, step 31, key o: C screen cell row 0 column 27 is A while JS is blank. At the same point C RNG begins rnd(5)=3 at mkroom.c:461; JavaScript instead records rn2(12)=7. The C trace then shows morguemon and collect_coords/makemon calls, while JS has no corresponding swarm call.

At the examined revision, js/apply.js:3822-3828 records note_unported("minion.c mkundead") and sets wakem without creating undead. js/mkroom.js:515-539 already implements morguemon. The other production call is nethack-c/upstream/src/spell.c:323, reached through js/spell.js:584, and passes revive_corpses=TRUE.
